subject.title: feat(self-host): local console sign-in without Cloudflare Access

question: Should the supported Docker self-host profile permit an operator to exchange the existing administrator bearer token for a 12-hour browser session when `CLAWROUTER_LOCAL_AUTH=enabled`?
rationale: The patch is intentionally bounded and preserves the existing default, but accepting a password-equivalent deployment token in a browser is a durable authentication and support-policy choice rather than a mechanical correctness decision.

options.title: Accept opt-in local sessions
options.body: Approve the documented opt-in shared-token model, keeping local authentication disabled by default and unavailable when Cloudflare Access is configured.

options.title: Keep API-only self-hosting
options.body: Decline the browser-session model and retain the existing bearer-token-only self-host workflow until a different local authentication design is selected.

recommendation.title: Accept opt-in local sessions
recommendation.body: Approve the documented opt-in shared-token model, keeping local authentication disabled by default and unavailable when Cloudflare Access is configured.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged self-host profile established the current API-only limitation and its deployment contract.
